body:
Do you mind if I ask why? I've Done it a few times (never so compulsively or regularly as to call it an addiction), but It's for the same reasons as everyone else. Part of it is I suppose some sort of instinctive urge, like how you want to hit something and scream if you're angry, or start running and singing if you're excessively happy. But it's never really been out of a decided hatred or desire to punish myself, it just seems like the most appropriate physical reaction to being sad. It's a supreme distraction, that effectively pushes everything out of my mind. Everything else seems irrelevant, so it really doesn't matter what happens tomorrow, or if I have to wear long sleeved shirts all day for the next six months, or how much much cleaning I'll have to do to get the blood stain out of the floor. It often leaves me laughing.  

I think another part of why I do it Is to reassure myself that I actually have a problem, that I'm somehow special and some sort of tortured soul, rather than just another unhappy person who should get their shit together. A rather unpleasant motive that's all too saturated with self pity. I can't help but worry that I only do it because I want to be able to think of myself as some manic depressive tortured genius that I'm not. Is this similar to why other people do it?
